rows.headline: How health insurance treats pollution-related illnesses in India
rows.hook: Smog claims growing space in hospital bills
rows.summary: Severe air pollution frequently triggers respiratory conditions like asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, leading to hospital admissions. Standard health insurance policies generally cover hospitalisation costs for these illnesses, but payouts depend heavily on specific policy terms. Policyholders must review waiting periods for pre-existing diseases, room rent caps, ICU sub-limits, and whether outpatient department costs are included. Understanding these clauses helps Indian retail investors and policyholders avoid unexpected out-of-pocket medical expenses during high-pollution months.
rows.why_it_matters: Pollution-linked hospital bills may surprise you without adequate policy riders
